finding.claim: list_users_sorted concatenates the raw $_GET['sort'] value into an ORDER BY clause, enabling SQL injection with blind data extraction from app.db. Reachability caveat: no caller of list_users_sorted exists in this directory, so exploitability depends on the wider application passing $_GET['sort'] into it.
finding.sink: PDO::query() on a string built by concatenation, list.php:6

trace.note: $sort = $_GET['sort'] ?? 'id' takes attacker-controlled input with no validation
"SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort concatenates the value into the SQL and passes it to PDO::query()

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, escaping, or cast on the path. PDO::query() runs a single statement, so stacked queries are not possible, but ORDER BY subqueries/CASE expressions still allow read-only blind extraction. list_users_safe (list.php:9-13) uses an allowlist and find_user (list.php:15-19) uses a bound parameter, so neither is affected. No caller found in the directory, so reachability is unconfirmed.

verdict.guard_found: none. list.php:5-6 concatenates $_GET['sort'] directly into the query with no allowlist, cast, or binding. The allowlist in list_users_safe (list.php:10-11) and the bound parameter in find_user (list.php:16-17) are in other functions and are not on this path.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: list.php:5 reads $_GET['sort'] and list.php:6 concatenates it into the ORDER BY clause with no guard. Whether an attacker can reach it is unknown, because list.php only defines functions and never calls list_users_sorted, so the sink is exploitable only if some web-reachable caller outside this directory passes the raw parameter through, and the candidate itself says that caller is unconfirmed.
